Kuvitus: älypuhelin latautuu puisella pö: Illustration: a smartphone charging on a wooden table in the evening. A cable runs from the phone to a white charger in a wall socket. The phone screen shows a battery symbol that is almost full of green, and a lightning bolt beside it. There is also a coffee cup on the table, and a lamp lights the wall.
Kaksi kytkentäkaaviota päällekkäin, ei m: Two circuit diagrams one above the other, not to scale. Upper: the battery discharges. The battery is on the left, the positive terminal, the long plate, at the top, and the lamp on the right. A purple current passes from the positive terminal of the battery along the upper wire to the lamp and along the lower wire to the negative terminal; inside the battery the current passes from the negative terminal to the positive terminal. An orange energy arrow points from the battery to the lamp. Lower: the battery is being charged. The charger is on the left and the battery on the right, both with the positive terminal at the top. The current passes from the positive terminal of the charger to the positive terminal of the battery, so inside the battery the current now passes from the positive terminal to the negative terminal, that is, in the opposite direction. The energy arrow points from the charger to the battery.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: purkuvirta I ampe: Graph to scale: the discharge current I in amperes as a function of time t in hours. The current is constant at 0.50 A from 0 to 4.0 h and then zero, when the battery is empty. The rectangle between the graph and the time axis is shaded; its area is the charge Q = It = 0.50 A · 4.0 h = 2.0 Ah.
Latauspiirin kytkentäkaavio, ei mittakaa: Circuit diagram of the charging circuit, not to scale. On the left is a charger whose voltage is U_ch, with the positive terminal at the top. In the upper wire are the resistance R of the charger and wires and an ammeter A. On the right is the battery bounded by a dashed line: inside it are the internal resistance R_s and the source voltage E, whose positive terminal is at the top. The terminals of the battery are at the edge of the dashed line, and a voltmeter V is connected between them; it shows the terminal voltage U. Purple current arrows pass from the positive terminal of the charger along the upper wire to the positive terminal of the battery, down through the battery and along the lower wire back to the negative terminal of the charger.
Potentiaalikuvaaja, pystyakseli mittakaa: Potential graph, vertical axis to scale, horizontal axis schematic: the loop of the charging circuit is traced from the negative terminal A of the charger through the charger, the resistor R and the battery back to A, when the voltage of the charger is 4.5 V, R = 0.40 ohms, the source voltage of the battery is 3.40 V and its internal resistance is 0.10 ohms, so the current is 2.2 A. In the charger the potential rises by 4.5 volts. In the resistor R it drops by 0.88 V, and at the positive terminal B of the battery it is 3.62 V, which is the terminal voltage. In the internal resistance of the battery it drops by 0.22 V to the value 3.40 V at point C, and at the source voltage of the battery by 3.40 V to zero. The current passes through the battery from the positive terminal to the negative terminal, so the potential drops in the battery.
Energiavirtakaavio mittakaavassa: nuolte: Energy flow diagram to scale: the width of the arrows is proportional to the energy. In a full charge from empty to full the charger delivers 9.0 Wh of energy, when the voltage of the charger is 4.5 V and the capacity of the battery is 2.0 Ah. Of this, 7.6 Wh is stored in the battery as chemical energy and continues as an arrow to the right. Two narrow arrows branch downwards: 1.1 Wh becomes internal energy of the charger and wires and 0.3 Wh internal energy of the battery, and they are transferred to the surroundings as heat.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: akun latausvirta: Graph to scale: the charging current I of a battery in amperes as a function of time t in hours, the grid spacing 0.5 h and 0.5 A. The current is 2.0 A from 0 to 1.5 h, then 1.0 A from 1.5 to 2.5 h, and zero after that.
